newsitem.title: UK: Eastbound dirty tanker rates firm, others mixed.
newsitem.headline: Eastbound dirty tanker rates firm, others mixed.

text.p: World crude tanker rates were mixed on Monday but the key Mideast Gulf sector remained buoyant amid healthy enquiries for late July loadings, brokers said.
Eastern rates for VLCCs firmed, with routes to Japan commanding an extra five Worldscale points after the Maersk Navarin was fixed to take 250,000 tonnes at the end of July for W75.
Singapore routes were also proving more lucrative than last week, reflected in the fixing of the Astra Beta off July 20 at W60, up from around W54 late last week.

Some brokers said they saw room for rates to firm even more with plenty of interest from charterers for third decade vessels but others said slow fixings last week had led to a build up in tonnage which should cap the market.

In the western hemisphere, West African rates held steady for both VLCCs and Suezmaxes but the North Sea was looking less attractive with rates for trans-Atlantic and Inter-UK Continent charters dipping between five and 10 points.
Brokers said the fall was expected given a slowdown in crude spot market activity with much of the July programmes placed and the August schedules not due out until later this week or early next.

U.S. oil company Sun paid W90 for the New Horizon to take 130,000 tonnes from the North Sea to the U.S. Atlantic Coast while BP paid W110 for an Aframax from the Flotta terminal to its Mobil joint venture refinery at Coryton.
Mediterranean cross rates were steady, with Suezmaxes pegged unchanged at W80 and Aframaxes at W120, brokers said.
